**Eq. 5 (page 3):**

$$L_3(\mathcal{C}) = L_2(\mathcal{C}) + \lambda \cdot L_1(\mathcal{C})$$

Here $\lambda$ is a weight on the auxiliary language-modeling objective (page 3). The terms are:

- **$L_2(\mathcal{C})$** is the supervised objective, Eq. 4 (page 3):
  $$L_2(\mathcal{C}) = \sum_{(x,y)} \log P(y \mid x^1, \ldots, x^m)$$
  where $P(y \mid x^1, \ldots, x^m) = \text{softmax}(h_l^m W_y)$ (Eq. 3, page 3).
- **$L_1$** is the language-modeling objective, Eq. 1 (page 3), applied here to the labeled dataset $\mathcal{C}$:
  $$L_1(\mathcal{U}) = \sum_i \log P(u_i \mid u_{i-k}, \ldots, u_{i-1}; \Theta)$$
  where $k$ is the context window size.

The authors add the language-modeling term because it improved generalization of the supervised model and sped up convergence (page 3). In their experiments, $\lambda$ was set to 0.5 (page 5).
